STUDENT INFORMATION GUIDE
Sample Case Study Document for RAG Pipeline
Fee Structure • Unit Registration • Session Reporting • Events
Academic Year 2025/2026
This is a sample case study document prepared for a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline
project. The content is based on JKUAT as a case study institution and covers sample fee structures, unit
registration procedures, session reporting guidelines, examination regulations, and upcoming university
events. This document is not an official JKUAT publication.

2. Session Reporting Guidelines
Session reporting is the formal process by which a student confirms their continued enrolment in a given
semester. It is mandatory for all registered JKUAT students, including those on attachment or special
programmes.
n DEADLINE: Session reporting must be completed before the end of the FIRST WEEK of
every semester

. Failure to session-report by this deadline will result in the student being marked
absent for that semester and may lead to academic suspension.
2.1 How to Session Report
Step 1
Log in to the JKUAT Student Portal at portal.jkuat.ac.ke using your registration number
and password.
Step 2
Navigate to Academics → Session Reporting from the main menu.
Step 3
Select the current academic year and semester.
Step 4
Verify that your personal details and programme information are correct. Report any
discrepancies to the Registrar's Office immediately.
Step 5
Click 'Confirm Session Report'

. A confirmation message and reference number will be
displayed and emailed to your university email address.
Step 6
Print or save a copy of the session report confirmation for your records.
2.2 Important Reminders
• Session reporting is available online from the first day of each semester.
• Students on academic leave or deferred study must also session-report to confirm return.
• Manual session reporting at the Registrar's Office is available for students with portal access issues.
• Session reporting does not replace unit registration; both must be completed independently.

3. Unit Registration Procedure
Unit registration is the process of enrolling in specific course units for a given semester. Only registered
units will appear in your official academic transcript and examination schedule.
n DEADLINE: All unit registrations must be completed before the end of the FOURTH (4th)
WEEK of the semester. Late registration will not be permitted after this date without special
approval from the Dean of the relevant Faculty.
3.1 Fee Payment Requirement Before Unit Registration
n MANDATORY FEE PAYMENT THRESHOLD:
A student must have paid a minimum of 75% of the total semester fees before they can register
units

. The system will automatically block unit registration for any student whose fee payment is
below this threshold. Part-payment arrangements below 75% will not be accepted as a basis for unit
registration.
3.2 Step-by-Step Unit Registration
Step 1
Ensure your semester fees are at least 75% paid. Check your fee balance on the Student
Portal under Finance → Fee Statement.
Step 2
Log in to the JKUAT Student Portal and navigate to Academics → Unit Registration.
Step 3
Select the current academic year, semester, and your programme.
Step 4
A list of recommended units based on your programme and year of study will appear

. Select
the units you wish to register.
Step 5
Review your selection and ensure you have not exceeded the maximum credit load for the
semester (typically 24 credit hours for undergraduate students).
Step 6
Click 'Submit Registration'. A confirmation with a unique registration number will be sent
to your university email.
Step 7
Print your unit registration card from the portal and keep it for future reference during
examinations.

4. Reasons Why a Student May Fail to Register Units
If a student is unable to complete unit registration on the portal, the cause is usually one or more of the
following. Identifying and resolving the specific issue early will prevent academic delays.
1
Fee Payment Below 75%
The most common reason. The system enforces a minimum payment of 75% of total semester fees
before allowing unit registration. Visit the Finance Office or pay via the official Paybill to clear the
deficit.
2
Session Reporting Not Completed
Students who have not session-reported for the current semester will be blocked from registering
units

. Complete session reporting first via the portal.
3
Outstanding Balance from Previous Semesters
Carried-forward arrears from prior semesters may lock your account. Contact the Finance Office for a
clearance letter or payment plan.
4
Academic Suspension or Probation
Students on academic suspension or under academic probation cannot register units until the Dean
lifts the restriction. Consult your Faculty Academic Office.
5
Incomplete Programme Clearance
Transfer students or those changing programmes may face a temporary lock while their new
programme details are being updated by the Registrar.
6
Missing Prerequisite Units
Some units require prior completion of specific prerequisite units

. If you have not passed the
prerequisite, the system will prevent registration. Confirm with your Department Head whether an
exemption is possible.
7
Portal Technical Issues
Occasional system downtime or browser compatibility issues may prevent successful registration. Try
a different browser, clear your cache, or visit the ICT Helpdesk at the Students' Centre.
8
Expired Student Status
Students whose maximum study duration has lapsed cannot register units without written approval
from the Senate. Apply for extension through your Faculty Dean.
9
Missing Biometric / Identity Verification
Year 1 students who have not completed biometric registration may be temporarily blocked

. Visit the
ICT Registration Centre to complete this process.

10
Household Fee Clearance Pending
On-campus students with outstanding household (hostel) fees may face restrictions. Settle the hostel
fee and obtain a clearance slip from the Hostels & Accommodation Office.
n If none of the above reasons apply and you still cannot register, proceed to the Academic
Registrar's Office with your student ID and fee receipt for manual assistance.

5. Examination Regulations & Fee Clearance
JKUAT maintains strict regulations governing student eligibility to sit for end-of-semester examinations.
Students must satisfy all the conditions below before being permitted into the examination room.
5.1 Household Fee Clearance
n CRITICAL REGULATION — HOUSEHOLD FEE:
A student who has not cleared their Household Fee (hostel / accommodation fee) in full will
NOT be permitted to sit for any University examinations for that semester.
This regulation applies to all students residing in JKUAT-managed accommodation

. Clearance must
be obtained from the Hostels & Accommodation Office and a clearance slip must be presented at
the examination venue together with the student identity card and unit registration card.
5.2 General Examination Eligibility Requirements
• Completed session reporting for the current semester.
• Registered all units for which examinations are to be sat.
• Attained a minimum class attendance of 75% for each registered unit.
• Cleared all outstanding household / hostel fees (for on-campus students).
• Submitted all continuous assessment tests (CATs) and assignments as required by the relevant
Department.
• Presented a valid Student Identity Card at the examination hall.

ed by the relevant
Department.
• Presented a valid Student Identity Card at the examination hall.
• Cleared any library fines or outstanding obligations as required.
5.3 Consequences of Non-Compliance
A student who does not meet the above requirements will be denied entry to the examination hall

. Such a
student will be awarded a grade of IC (Incomplete) or AB (Absent), which may lead to a fail grade upon
processing. Supplementary or special examinations may be applied for through the Dean's Office in
accordance with the University's Academic Policy.

7. Upcoming University Events
JKUAT regularly hosts international academic conferences, workshops, and seminars that bring together
scholars, researchers, and industry professionals. Students and faculty are encouraged to participate
actively in these events to foster academic excellence and networking.

7.1 Conference Overview
The 2nd International Conference on Mathematics and Physical Sciences (ICMPS 2026) is a prestigious
biennial event hosted by the JKUAT College of Pure and Applied Sciences

. The conference brings
together mathematicians, physicists, chemists, statisticians, and data scientists from across Africa and the
world to share cutting-edge research, forge collaborations, and advance the frontiers of knowledge in the
mathematical and physical sciences.
